svg.aria-label: How to write ક — ણ — શ: 3 letters, ક, ણ, શ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ક — ણ — શ
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ક, ણ, શ (gujarati). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ક: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ક animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ણ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ણ animation, first through third SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; શ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, શ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: ક: The teaching app animates ક as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper right, circles left around the upper loop, continues diagonally down-right through the middle crossing, then circles the rounded lower body and finishes at the lower left. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path sweeps a separate diagonal cross-stroke from lower left to upper right. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the upper loop, central diagonal, rounded lower body, and crossing diagonal, but its printed loops are broader and the crossing more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's joined-loop-body-before-diagonal-cross-stroke order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loops, diagonal, and terminals differently. ણ: The teaching app animates ણ as three ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path descends the left spine, then sweeps through the hooked lower tail. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path circles the separate rounded middle bowl. It lifts again and its third SVG path descends the tall right spine before turning through the lower foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the hooked body, middle bowl, and tall right spine, but its printed body is broader, its tail descends below the baseline, and its joins and foot are more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-middle-bowl-before-right-spine order and two-lift evidence while fitting all three runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, join, or slant the body, hook, bowl, spine, and terminals differently. શ: The teaching app animates શ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper right, circles the small upper loop, then continues through the broad lower body and into its lower-right tail. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper loop, broad lower body, tail, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed body is wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, body, tail, spine, foot, and terminals differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 2 of 3 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ક animation, first and second SVG paths
Letter 2: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ણ animation, first through third SVG paths
Letter 3: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, શ animation, first and second SVG paths
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
